To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a DQ assessment methodology has been defined and implemented in a tool; (2) DQ is not a single concept but it can be decomposed into several components; (3) the proposed methodology allows to assess and monitor the DQ of a data source; and (4) the proposed methodology is based on a set of metrics and indicators that can be used for DQ assessment and monitoring.

(i) a DQ framework is needed to support the DQ management in an organization and to provide a common language for the communication between different actors involved in DQ; (ii) a DQ assessment methodology is required to evaluate DQ of data in an organization; (iii) a DQ monitoring methodology is necessary to support the continuous monitoring of DQ in an organization

a) the DQ assessment process should be based on a set of quality indicators, that can be grouped in two categories, namely data quality indicators (DQIs) and data quality dimensions (DQDs), and that b) a data quality monitoring process should be based upon a set of data quality metrics (DQMs), that can be grouped into three categories: data quality metrics for data completeness, data quality metrics for accuracy, and data quality metrics for consistency.

the development of an integrated framework for DQ assessment and monitoring, and the definition of a methodology and an associated tool that support the framework.

the assessment and monitoring process should be considered as a continuous process, and that the quality of data should be assessed and monitored by using a multidimensional approach, which considers the data from the point of view of its source, its use, the context in which it is used and the users who are using it.
